News.title: Brit tourist, 47, pulled unconscious from sea at holiday hotspot resort & given life-saving CPR on beach
News.content:
KISS OF LIFE Brit tourist, 47, pulled unconscious from sea at holiday hotspot resort & given life-saving CPR on beach

A BRIT tourist has been pulled unconscious from the sea and given life-saving CPR on the beach at a Spanish holiday hotspot.

The holidaymaker, 47, was rushed to hospital after being spotted floating in the water in Majorca before suffering cardiac arrest.



He began having a heart attack after lifeguards rescued him from the sea in Santa Ponsa near Magaluf just after midday, reports say.



Off-duty firefighters also helped first responders revive him after they found he had no pulse.

He was brought into stable condition at the scene and later rushed to Son Espases Hospital in the Majorcan capital Palma.

The tourist is understood to be a Brit who was born in Pakistan.

The terrifying ordeal unfolded just after midday on Thursday.

It kicked off when lifeguards spotted a man who wasn’t moving in the water from a watch tower on the beach.

One of them raced into the sea to bring him out with the help of other tourists and locals.

News.title: Heartbroken dad’s agony as ex-soldier son, 29, is crushed to death by his own truck on ‘dream job’
News.content:
FREAK TRAGEDY Heartbroken dad’s agony as ex-soldier son, 29, is crushed to death by his own truck on ‘dream job’

AN ex-soldier and HGV driver was crushed to death by his own truck’s cargo in a freak tragedy, an inquest heard.

Tom Willis, 29, died after one of two tractors he was delivering rolled backwards off his lorry and trapped him underneath.





The former soldier, had travelled 250 miles from Tiverton, Devon, to a yard in Alltami, Flintshire, when the horror unfolded.

An inquest was told that Tom shouted: “Woah, woah, woah” moments before he was crushed.

A two-day hearing in Ruthin heard the 29-year-old had been delivering the tractors when one rolled off the back of the vehicle.

Home Office forensic pathologist Dr Brian Rodgers said Tom would have died rapidly from his injuries.



The cause of death was recorded as crush asphyxia.

Former North Wales Police vehicle examiner Peter Jones told jurors CCTV footage showed Tom carrying two chain ratchet load binders outside the site at 5.51am.

Mr Jones said he believed Tom had removed the chains before entering the yard in preparation for unloading the tractors.

The jury later returned a narrative conclusion saying a “combination of factors” caused one of the units to roll backwards, trapping him and inflicting “severe crush injuries”.



Speaking after the hearing, devastated dad Paul Willis described the tragedy as “wrong place, wrong time”.

He said: “It was just a genuine mistake. One hundred percent – wrong place wrong time.

“Tom was a big believer in ‘what is done is done – move on.’ He never held grudges.

“If you had an argument with him, even myself, the next night we’d be in the pub having a drink together.

“Everybody liked him. He got on so well with all the customers no matter where he worked.”



Paul said his son first discovered his love of driving while serving in the Army.

He added: “Tom started his driving career in the Army. He loved it in Europe doing all the big tank movements.

“When came back, we got him a job driving tankers.

“Within two years he was running all the lorries for that company.

“He was so positive and just always wanted to move on, to improve himself – to climb the ladder.”



Paul said Tom had been thrilled after landing a role with David Mouland Haulage.

He said: “When he got the job he was doing, with David Mouland Haulage, he told everyone it was the job of his dreams.

“He loved it – it’s exactly where he wanted to be.”

The grieving dad said the family are now trying to come to terms with the tragedy.

He added: “It’s very emotional, obviously we’re learning more now than we knew.



“There will never be closure, but hopefully we can draw a line under this part of the proceedings and get on with our lives.”

News.title: Vid shows China CHANGED spelling of Marco Rubio to allow him to join Trump state visit after he was banned from country
News.content:
MARCO NEW-BIO Vid shows China CHANGED spelling of Marco Rubio to allow him to join Trump state visit after he was banned from country

CHINA has secretly changed the spelling of Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s name — handing itself a bureaucratic loophole to let him into the country despite a years-long travel ban.

Beijing quietly swapped out a Chinese character used to represent the first syllable of Rubio’s surname shortly after he took office last year.





China said Tuesday it would not stop Rubio — making his first-ever visit to the country for talks with President Xi Jinping — from flying to Beijing aboard Air Force One with Donald Trump.

“The sanctions target Mr. Rubio’s words and deeds when he served as a US senator concerning China,” Chinese embassy spokesman Liu Pengyu told Agence France-Presse (AFP).

Two diplomats told AFP they believed the name change was a deliberate workaround — letting China bypass sanctions that were imposed under the old spelling.

Rubio was banned from entering China in 2020 after he called out Beijing’s treatment of the Uyghur Muslim minority in the Xinjiang region.



When pressed on the name change last year, China’s foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told state media she “had not noticed it but would look into it,” The Guardian reported.

The name drama played out as Trump touched down in Beijing to a lavish welcome ceremony — the start of a two-day state visit carrying major consequences for the world’s two biggest economies.

Waiting on the tarmac were China’s Vice President Han Zheng, US Ambassador to China David Perdue, Chinese Ambassador to the US Xie Feng, and China’s Executive Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs Ma Zhaoxu.

Along with Rubio, Trump was joined by a heavyweight delegation of top business leaders — including Apple boss Tim Cook, Tesla billionaire Elon Musk, and Nvidia boss Jensen Huang.



Musk’s six-year-old son X Æ A-Xii also showed up clutching an adorable dragon bag.

First Lady Melania Trump was notably absent, despite joining her husband when he last visited China in 2017.

Also on the trip were Trump’s son Eric Trump and daughter-in-law Lara Trump, alongside Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Xi Jinping put Donald Trump on notice — warning that a war between the world’s two superpowers could be catastrophic.

Trump and Xi walked past a grand military ceremony before sitting down for two hours of crunch talks in the capital.



The two leaders discussed their tariff truce and Taiwan — with Xi declaring the nations must be “partners, not rivals.”

But Xi warned the two powers could clash if they failed to agree on “the most important issue” in US-China relations.

A spokesperson for Beijing’s foreign ministry said, “President Xi stressed to President Trump that the Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations.

“If it is handled properly, the bilateral relationship will enjoy overall stability.

“Otherwise, the two countries will have clashes and even conflicts, putting the entire relationship in great jeopardy.”

News.title: Did secret UK nuke tests give us cancer? The ‘human lab rats’ haunted by baby deaths & rotten bones hunting for answers
News.content:
MOMENTS after the five-second countdown ended, Brian Unthank recalls a white flash so bright that he could see the bones, tendons and blood vessels in his fists – despite having his eyes firmly shut.

A humongous fireball then rolled up into the sky, followed by a thick, black shock-wave that threw his body across the beach “like a rag doll” and a heat similar to a “steelworks blast furnace” washed over his skin.





Dusting himself off from where he fell on Christmas Island, 7,500 miles from Britain in the Pacific Ocean, RAF cook Brian seemed unharmed and thought “what the effing hell was that?” as he looked around at the other “dismayed and shocked” servicemen.

Brian, now 88, was one of 39,000 British and Commonwealth military personnel who witnessed 45 atomic and hydrogen bomb tests and hundreds more radioactive experiments at multiple locations during the 15 years until 1967, as part of our post-war nuclear weapons test programme.

The majority, including Brian, say they had no idea they were about to witness the nuclear tests until the detonations took place and claim they, alongside with their descendants, have developed a plethora of deadly and damaging health problems because of it. The MOD strongly refutes claims of harm.

Known as the Nuclear Blood Scandal, the surviving veterans – who were initially unable to tell anyone about what happened due to the Official Secrets Act – have been campaigning for compensation and recognition.

They allege military officials didn’t warn them of any risk, insisting they were “absolutely safe and in no danger”, yet experts have since revealed exposure to the radiation and materials contaminated with ionised debris “damages organs and DNA within cells”.

Nuclear technology historian Bo Jacobs states: “Depending on how high your dose is, you could become sick within minutes. If you’re further away, you could develop cancers because of the harm.”

Brian was 19 years old when he witnessed two hydrogen bombs, roughly located around 20 miles away during each test, which had a combined yield equivalent to 320 Hiroshima bombs, and he has since suffered with horrifying consequences.

Within weeks of returning to the UK, blood began pouring from his mouth, and all of his teeth and part of his jaw had to be removed.





He’s since had 98 skin cancers removed and battles bladder and a rare form of prostate cancer.

Brian and his first wife also suffered 13 late-term miscarriages. Of his surviving six children, one was born with a double womb, a second with two holes in his heart, a third with an eye movement disorder and a final with spinal and internal problems requiring medication for life.

He also blames the blasts for one grandchild needing a deadly black melanoma removed at 14 months old and another’s teeth “turning to chalk” without reason – something suffered by other nuclear test veterans.

In spite of his heartbreaking issues, Brian, of Kent, who appears in the new documentary Our Planet, The People, My Blood, which is now out in cinemas, tells us: “I consider myself one of the lucky ones.

“We have suffered the least problems compared to other veterans – some have lost children, others have had leukaemia, heart problems and all sorts of dreadful diseases.

“This is hammering down into our bloodstreams and will be in our bloodstream for the next 500 years, yet the Government says we were ‘safe and unharmed’.

“If I had not been harmed, why have I had all of these personal problems? In addition to those running down to my family. It has been the same and worse for other veterans, too.

“This is Britain’s biggest scandal – the Post Office Scandal was terrible, but this has beset us for 70 years, and successful Governments have ignored us and pushed it under the carpet.

“I could drop dead tomorrow. I believe the Government is waiting for us nuclear test veterans to pass away, and then will say, ‘Oh dear, we should have done something’.

“They are also forgetting our descendants, who are all taking the cudgel on our behalf. We all want an apology from Keir Starmer and to be rightly compensated.”



Brian’s testimony is among many British veterans and campaigners, who refer to themselves as the ‘Labrats’, as they battle to have their military medical records released by the MOD to discover the full extent of their health problems and what was known about them at the time.

One of them, John Morris, 88, of Rochdale, Lancashire, blames the death of his four-month-old Steven on his exposure while on Christmas Island.

He and his wife, Betty, were initially questioned on suspicion of murdering their baby, who was found dead in his cot, by police before being released without charge.

Initially, Steven’s death was ruled to be due to a form of pneumonia, but John is adamant his son was “perfectly healthy” and showed no symptoms of ill health.

It took 50 years and a Freedom of Information Act request to obtain a coroner’s report that suggested Steven’s lungs may not have developed properly, which John blames on his exposure to radiation.

A 2014 University of Liverpool study reported that children of the nuclear test veterans experienced 10 times the normal rate of birth defects and were five times more likely to die as infants due to a “genomic instability” in the DNA passed down from their fathers.

Damage to DNA is known to cause mutations in genes, which regulate cell growth, repair and unregulated division, can lead to cancers and genetic defects.

The MOD disputes claims of veterans’ offspring being at increased risk, stating there is “no definitive evidence”.



And a 2022 study, in Scientific Reports, found there was “no significant increase” in the frequency of “newly arising genetic changes” for the offspring of the nuclear test veteran community. However, they could not conclusively rule on whether health issues were related to “random occurrence” or radiation exposure.

Veterans argue that the likelihood of so many of them and their offspring suffering health problems, often battling the same issues, that it’s impossible for it to happen by chance.

John, who witnessed four nuclear explosions while serving in the Royal Engineers, worked handling contaminated clothing with recycled contaminated water.

He now suffers from a blood disorder and has cancer. He calls himself and fellow comrades “human guinea pigs”.

Alan Owen, founder of campaign group Labrats, is the son of the late Royal Navy man James, who witnessed 24 detonations in 78 days and died from a heart attack aged 52.

His death was caused by a genetic condition, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy – yet after the family had genetic testing to “find the code in the gene” that caused it, there was nothing.

“It didn’t show in the first panel, so something else has caused it,” Alan says, suggesting his father’s exposure to radiation was to blame.

Alan claims his siblings have also been blighted by health issues – he suffered a near-fatal cardiac arrest aged 51, and his brother died of one aged 31.

His sister Laura Jackson was also born blind in one eye, needed operations on her jaw, sinuses and head, lost her teeth, suffered multiple miscarriages and has had cancer three times.

Filmmaker Daniel Everitt-Lock, 35, considers it “a gigantic scandal” and says it was “well-hidden” for many decades due to the Official Secrets Act.



That silence was true for Brian, who didn’t tell his first wife what he experienced, despite suffering multiple health issues, which began aged 20.

His problems began weeks after returning home from Christmas Island, known locally as Kiritimati, when “blood started gushing from my mouth” without reason.

“They found my gums had receded right the way to the base of the roots, my teeth top and bottom had to be removed and part of my lower jaw,” Brian says.

“I was told it was a severe case of gingivitis (gum disease), but many of the other veterans also lost teeth and were told the same story – is it not strange we all suffered the same thing?”

Brian blames his exposure to two detonations. He claims he was told nothing about the first bomb test other than to sit on the beach with his fists covering his eyes and his knees by his chest.

He says: “That was the sum of our instructions. We were told absolutely nothing.

“I was 20 metres away and my ‘safety clothing’ was a short-sleeved shirt, a pair of shorts, socks, shoes and a beret. That was your cover.”

The second test he witnessed was a 3.8 megatonne bomb – the equivalent of 3.8 million tonnes of TNT – which was so powerful it “sucked up half the ocean before dumping it on the island”.



“We were showered in heavily radiated water, I remember seeing all of this green rain coming down but also rising up to the sky at the same time,” he says.

“Then we breathed heavily ionised, radiated air, drank ionised radiated water and ate ionised radiated fish, yet the MOD say we were ‘unharmed.’”

The documentary also covers the damage caused by the nuclear weapons industry to “millions of people” across the world.

Britain was far from the only country performing tests, but other countries, including America, France and Russia, have compensated exposed veterans and personnel.

Additionally, Fiji has paid ex-servicemen who were at Christmas Island during Britain’s tests.

Veterans claim they have been “treated very badly”. It took until late 2023 for them or their next-of-kin to finally receive recognition through a Nuclear Veteran Test Medal. Since then, 5,000 have been issued.

It followed multiple refusals because the men “didn’t meet the risk or rigour for a medal”, they claim, which the ex-servicemen “found incredibly disrespectful”.

Brian adds: “When the medal did arrive, it came in a jiffy bag in pieces, and you had to buy a clip to sew the ribbon onto and put it together. It was almost a smack in the face.”



It’s estimated that around 1,500 of the 20,000 UK nuclear test veterans, who served in Australia, Fiji and the Pacific Islands, are alive today, and their battle for compensation goes on.

Documentarian Daniel adds: “It’s far more ruining than the Post Office Scandal and has affected a great many more people, even in the UK alone.

“The nuclear test veterans receiving medals was a very good thing, but it’s nowhere near enough for what they have been through for the last seven decades. This should only be the beginning.”

Labrats have two goals – a Special Justice tribunal, which would have the power to impose judicial and adjudicatory powers, compel witnesses and evidence and “crucially… award compensation”.

They also want a Public Inquiry into what it considers to be an “institutionalised culture of obstruction, obfuscation, failures of disclosure, and denial towards victims of injustice at the hands of the state”.

Last month, The Mirror revealed documents that found veterans were exposed to nuclear fallout on Christmas Island despite multiple previous MOD denials.

It showed fish were seven times more radioactive than normal, alongside contamination to the water they drank and swam in and the air they breathed.

Veterans are also fighting to obtain their full medical records; some say they have received documents, but large sections are redacted.

They also want records regarding blood and urine samples taken during their deployment, which would reveal radiation levels. They are currently held in a database known as Merlin, which “has not been declassified” due to containing information “ranging from unclassified to Top Secret”.

The MOD told us that compensation and pension benefits are available through the War Pensions Scheme, in addition to help through other funds.



However, each case is considered on its own merits – and some veterans say they have been denied a war pension.

A MOD spokesperson told us: “We recognise the huge contribution that Nuclear Test Veterans have made to national security.

“This government is committed to working with veterans and listening to their concerns, and the Minister for Veterans and People meets regularly with the campaign group Labrats.

“A long-term study found that nuclear test veterans are no more likely to have cancer or die early than similar military personnel, and overall rates are lower than among the general public.

“Similarly, there is no definitive evidence that children of nuclear test veterans have an increased number of genetic mutations or health conditions than the general public.”

Find out where to watch Our Planet, The People, My Blood at: www.atomicblood.com.

News.title: Paranoid thug destroys pub in stolen bulldozer over fears his wife was romping with regulars
News.content:
A PARANOID thug destroyed a pub in a bulldozer rampage over fears his wife was sleeping with regulars.

Daniel Morgan, 35, had been drinking in the boozer when he flew into a rage at the punters over “banter” about his marriage breakdown.





Morgan wrongly believed in a “paranoid way” that his wife had been having affairs with the landlord and regulars – and planned a revenge attack.

Prosecutor Jason Howells said he left the pub before messaging landlord Christopher Common to say: “Be careful, you can’t stop a dozer.”

The court heard Morgan also messaged: “It will be a drive-thru” after he left The New Inn in Cefn Rhigos near Aberdare, South Wales.

Mr Howells said Morgan went to his father’s farm before he took the vintage Hanomag D600 bulldozer without permission in December.

His father Phillip watched in horror from a window as his son ploughed through an Isuzu truck on the farm – and quickly called his nephew for help.

The pair made their way to the local boozer to alert the owners as punters exited into the car park when Morgan turned up.



Merthyr Tydfil Crown Court heard Morgan rammed into the porch causing £22,280.43 of damage – and costing £7,000 lost revenue for the weekend.

Morgan’s father Phillip “heroically” attempted to cut the diesel pipe on the engine in a bid to stop his son’s “revenge attack.”

Mr Howell’s said: “The defendant moved the bulldozer from side to side preventing anyone from getting close to it.”



The court heard Morgan left the pub to drive to the family home he had lived in with his estranged wife.

His father, uncle and cousin attempted to block the road with a digger before he finally came to stop “covered in blood.”

The court heard police arrived to find Morgan “heavily intoxicated” in the driver’s seat while bleeding from his head and hands.

Morgan was taken to hospital where he told officers: “This is all because my ex won’t let me see the kids.”

He also said he “saw red” when he drove the bulldozer over his family’s vehicles.



The court heard victim Mr Common said he believed Morgan was not in the right frame of mind due to “personal issues.”

Mr Howells said: “He does not believe the defendant would have acted this way and caused the damage if he had been in the right frame of mind.”

The landlord said he believed Morgan was “acting weird” due to his mental health – and would usually help anyone in the village.

The court heard Morgan had began drinking six pints a day and using £100 of cocaine every day due to his relationship breakdown.

Morgan, of Rhigos, Aberdare, pleaded guilty to aggravated vehicle taking, dangerous driving; and damaging property being reckless as to whether life is endangered.



Judge Celia Hughes said Morgan was finally stopped due to the “incredible bravery” of his own family members.

She said: “What you did on the night of this incident will have grave affects on you and others close to you for the rest of your life.

“You acted out of revenge albeit impetuously that night and I accept that was out of character for you.”

Morgan was jailed for three years and four months and disqualified from driving for four years and must take an extended test.

He was ordered to pay £10,000 to Mr Common.



After the sentence, Ryan Randall, of the CPS, said: “Daniel Morgan showed a complete disregard for the safety of other people who could have been in the pub.
